title: Demystifying Instruction Mixing for Fine-tuning Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how mixing different instruction-tuning datasets affects large language model performance. The authors ask whether combining general-purpose chat instructions, NLP downstream-task instructions, and coding instructions produces uniform gains or whether some mixtures help specific capabilities while hurting others.

The study fine-tunes LLaMA-2 7B and 13B on combinations of three public instruction datasets: Alpaca (general chat), P3 (NLP task reformulations), and CodeAlpaca (code generation). The evaluation is entirely computational and uses standard NLP benchmarks, HumanEval for code generation, and FLASK/GPT-4 based alignment-skill scoring. No human learners, teachers, or schools are involved.

The main finding is that specialized instruction data improves performance in its own domain, but mixed datasets do not always improve all outcomes. In particular, P3-style NLP instructions can reduce alignment/chat ability, while code instructions can improve both coding and alignment when combined with general instructions. The paper also reports that performance depends on model size and instruction ratio, with larger models benefiting more from diverse mixtures.

identified_tools.name: LLaMA
identified_tools.description: Meta's LLaMA family of large language models for general-purpose language understanding and generation, including instruction-tuned variants.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper fine-tunes LLaMA-2 7B and 13B models with different instruction mixtures (Alpaca, CodeAlpaca, P3) and evaluates NLP, code, and alignment performance.

findings.finding_summary: Across zero-shot NLP and code benchmarks, specialized instruction datasets improved performance on their respective task areas, but combining all instruction types did not uniformly improve all tasks. For example, P3 improved NLP averages and CodeAlpaca improved HumanEval pass rates, while some mixtures performed best depending on model size (7B vs 13B).
findings.measure: NLP benchmarks (ARC, Winogrande, PIQA, MMLU, RACE, HellaSwag) and HumanEval pass@1/pass@10

findings.finding_summary: Mixing P3 data caused a drop in alignment skills of -2.8 points for LLaMA-2-7B and -3.6 points for LLaMA-2-13B on the FLASK-based GPT-4 alignment evaluation. The authors conclude that P3 has a negative impact on fine-tuning chatbot LLMs.
findings.measure: FLASK alignment skill scores averaged over eight dimensions

quality_tier_rationale: This is a controlled experimental study that systematically compares multiple fine-tuning mixtures and evaluates them with benchmark tasks and a GPT-4-based alignment rubric. It is not an RCT in the education sense, but the methodology is clear and reproducible.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports meaningful performance changes, including negative alignment effects from P3 mixing, but the effects are reported as benchmark-score differences rather than standardized effect sizes. The educational relevance is indirect because the study is on general LLM fine-tuning, not K-12 teacher coaching.
